ob-stronger.alt: Valid order block checklist: the move broke structure (BOS), left a fair value gap, the zone is unmitigated, and it agrees with the higher-timeframe trend
ob-stronger.caption: A stronger order block ticks all four boxes: break of structure, an imbalance (FVG), unmitigated, and in line with the higher timeframe.

ob-trading.alt: How to trade an order block: wait for price to return to the zone, confirm with a lower-timeframe change of character, stop loss beyond the order block, target the next liquidity
ob-trading.caption: Trading an order block: wait for the return, confirm on a lower timeframe, place the stop beyond the zone and target the next liquidity.

ob-vs-sd.h2: Order block vs supply and demand
ob-vs-sd.alt: Order block vs supply and demand zone on the same chart: the order block is one candle and tighter, the demand zone covers the whole base and is wider
ob-vs-sd.caption: The same move marked two ways: an order block uses one candle, a supply and demand zone covers the whole base.

bos-close.alt: Break of structure: a candle body closing beyond the swing high is a real BOS; a wick that pokes through and closes back inside is a liquidity sweep
bos-close.caption: Count a break when the candle body closes beyond the level. A wick through and a close back inside is usually a liquidity sweep.

bos-internal.alt: Internal vs swing structure: inside a higher-timeframe uptrend the pullback makes its own internal CHoCH, which only ends the pullback before the swing high breaks
bos-internal.caption: Swing structure is the big highs and lows. An internal CHoCH inside the pullback often only marks the end of the pullback, not a reversal.

fvg-test.alt: Fair value gap test results: a limit entry at the 50% consequent encroachment level won 31% of trades at 1:2 versus 28% for random zones over 23,773 FVGs on Gold and EURUSD
fvg-test.caption: Our test of 23,773 FVGs: a limit order at the 50% level (CE) beat random zones of the same size in 8 of 8 tests; a plain touch-and-bounce did not.

fvg-plan.alt: How to trade a fair value gap: higher-timeframe direction, an FVG left by the move that broke structure, entry on the return into the gap, stop beyond it and target the next liquidity
fvg-plan.caption: An FVG plan in four steps: direction first, the gap left by the break of structure, the return into it, then stop and target.

liq-where.alt: Where liquidity sits on a forex chart: buy stops above equal highs and the previous day high, sell stops below equal lows and under a trendline
liq-where.caption: Liquidity pools: above equal highs and the previous day's high, below equal lows and along trendlines that many traders draw.

liq-stop.alt: Stop loss placement and liquidity: a stop exactly at the obvious low gets swept, a stop with a buffer below the level survives the sweep
liq-stop.caption: Do not place your stop exactly at the obvious level. Give it a buffer so a liquidity sweep does not take you out.

smc-pd.alt: Premium and discount in SMC: the range from swing low to swing high split at the 50% equilibrium, with the OTE optimal trade entry zone at 62–79% of the retracement
smc-pd.caption: Above 50% of the swing is premium, below is discount. OTE is the deep 62–79% part of the pullback; combine it with an order block or FVG.

smc-kz.alt: ICT killzones in Pakistan time (winter): London killzone about 12–3 PM PKT and New York killzone about 5–8 PM PKT, after the Asian range
smc-kz.caption: Killzones are the busy hours when sweeps and displacement happen most: about 12–3 PM and 5–8 PM PKT in winter.

pa-candles.h2: 1. Candles: what each bar tells you
pa-candles.alt: Reading candlesticks in price action: a big bullish body, a long lower wick, a pin bar at support and a bullish engulfing candle
pa-candles.caption: What each candle says: the body shows who won, the wick shows rejection, a pin bar at a level and an engulfing candle show a shift.

pa-mtf.alt: Multiple timeframe analysis in price action: H4 gives the trend and level, H1 shows the pullback to the level, M15 gives the engulfing entry with a tight stop
pa-mtf.caption: Top-down: the higher timeframe gives direction and levels, the middle timeframe the setup, the lower timeframe the entry candle.

pa-triggers.alt: Four price action entry triggers at a level: rejection wick, engulfing candle, breakout and retest, and false breakout
pa-triggers.caption: Four entry triggers at a level: rejection, engulfing, breakout and retest, false breakout. Act only after the candle closes.

sb-setup.h2: What the Silver Bullet setup is
sb-setup.alt: ICT Silver Bullet setup inside the one-hour window: a sweep of a nearby high, displacement with a market structure shift, entry in the fair value gap, stop beyond the sweep
sb-setup.caption: Inside the hour: a sweep of nearby liquidity, a strong move the other way with a structure shift, then an entry in the FVG it leaves.

sb-markets.alt: Which ICT Silver Bullet window to trade from Pakistan: London 1–2 PM for EURUSD, GBPUSD and Gold; New York AM 8–9 PM for Gold and US indices; New York PM 12–1 AM
sb-markets.caption: Which window suits which market: London for EURUSD, GBPUSD and Gold; New York AM for Gold and US indices; New York PM is quieter.

rm-stop.h2: Rule 2: place the stop loss first
rm-stop.alt: Where to place a stop loss in forex: beyond the swing low for a buy with a small buffer; the stop is a chart decision, then the lot size follows
rm-stop.caption: The stop goes where the trade idea is proven wrong, beyond the swing with a buffer. If it is too far, trade a smaller lot or skip.

rm-lot.h2: Rule 3: let the lot size come from the risk and the stop
rm-lot.alt: Lot size formula: money at risk divided by stop distance times value per lot; $10 risk with a 25 pip stop on EURUSD is 0.04 lot, with a $5 stop on Gold it is 0.02 lot
rm-lot.caption: Same $10 risk, different lots: the lot comes from the risk and the stop distance, never the other way round.

rr-calc.alt: How to calculate risk:reward: a 40 pip take profit divided by a 20 pip stop loss gives 1:2; a full win is +2R and a full loss is −1R
rr-calc.caption: Divide the take-profit distance by the stop-loss distance: 40 ÷ 20 = 1:2. A win is +2R, a loss −1R.

rr-exp.alt: Trading expectancy example: 100 trades with 40% winners at 1:2 give +80R minus 60R, a net +20R or +0.2R per trade
rr-exp.caption: With 40% winners at 1:2, expectancy is +0.2R per trade: about +20% over 100 trades at 1% risk, before costs.

rr-real.h2: A big RR is not automatically better
rr-real.alt: Realistic take profit: a 1:2 target placed before strong resistance is reached more often than a 1:5 target beyond it
rr-real.caption: Put the target just before the next real level and accept the RR the chart gives. A 1:5 beyond strong resistance is rarely hit.

dd-what.alt: What drawdown is in forex: an account grows from $1,000 to a $1,200 peak and falls to $960, a $240 or 20% drawdown measured from the peak
dd-what.caption: Drawdown is measured from the highest point: $1,200 down to $960 is a 20% drawdown, even though the account is only 4% below its start.

dd-bal-eq.alt: Balance vs equity drawdown: the balance line moves only when trades close, while equity also counts floating losses and shows the deeper real drawdown
dd-bal-eq.caption: Balance counts closed trades only. Equity also counts floating losses, so it shows the real drawdown that prop firms and margin calls use.

dd-streaks.alt: Losing streaks in forex: over 100 trades a 50% win rate has about a 55% chance of 6 losses in a row, and 10 losses cost 9.6% at 1% risk but 40.1% at 5% risk
dd-streaks.caption: Long losing runs are normal even for good strategies. What they cost depends only on your risk per trade.

pf-math.alt: Prop firm challenge maths: five losses in a row at 1% risk reach the 5% daily loss limit, while at 0.5% risk the same streak costs only 2.5%
pf-math.caption: Five losses at 1% break a 5% daily limit; at 0.5% the same streak costs 2.5%. Passing is about small, steady risk.

pf-plan.alt: A simple prop firm challenge risk plan: risk 0.25–0.5% per trade, a personal daily stop of 2–2.5%, stop after 2 losses a day and after 4–5% down in a week
pf-plan.caption: A simple plan: tiny risk per trade, your own daily stop at half the firm's limit, and hard stops for the day and the week.

ps-traps.alt: The four trading psychology traps: FOMO buying after the run, moving the stop loss, revenge trading with bigger lots, and overtrading without a setup
ps-traps.caption: The four traps that break good plans: FOMO, moving the stop, revenge trading and overtrading.

ps-journal.alt: Trading journal template: date, pair, setup, result in R and emotion for every trade, plus a weekly review that shows which rule breaks cost the most
ps-journal.caption: Write every trade in a journal with the setup, the result in R and your emotion, then review it every week.

gold-drivers.alt: What moves the Gold price: the US dollar, Fed interest rates, US data such as NFP and CPI, and risk sentiment as a safe haven
gold-drivers.caption: Four things that move Gold: the US dollar, the Fed and rates, big US data releases, and the market's risk mood.

gold-time.h2: When to trade it from Pakistan
gold-time.alt: Best time to trade Gold in Pakistan: the London–New York overlap, about 6–10 PM PKT in winter and 5–9 PM PKT in summer
gold-time.caption: Gold moves best in London and the London–New York overlap: about 6–10 PM PKT in winter and 5–9 PM in summer.

pip-value.alt: Pip value in forex: $10 per pip for 1.00 lot, $1 for 0.10 lot and $0.10 for 0.01 lot on USD-quoted pairs; on USDJPY at 150 one lot is about $6.67 per pip
pip-value.caption: Pip value: $10, $1 or $0.10 per pip on USD-quoted pairs depending on the lot; on other pairs it changes with the price.

pip-money.alt: From pips to money: 25 pips stop loss × $10 pip value per lot × 0.04 lot = $10 at risk, and the same formula turned around gives the lot size
pip-money.caption: Money at risk = stop in pips × pip value × lots. 25 × $10 × 0.04 = $10; turn it around to get the lot size for any risk.

spread-chart.alt: Bid and ask on a forex chart: the chart shows the bid, the ask sits above it by the spread; a buy opens at the ask and closes at the bid
spread-chart.caption: The chart shows the bid; the ask is above it by the spread. A buy opens at the ask and closes at the bid, so every trade starts slightly negative.

spread-widen.alt: When do forex spreads widen: at the daily rollover around 3 AM Pakistan time in winter, around high-impact US news and in quiet hours
spread-widen.caption: Spreads widen at the rollover, around big news and in quiet hours. Illustration of a typical day in Pakistan time.

swap-mt5.h2: How to find and calculate it in MT5
swap-mt5.alt: How to find and calculate swap in MT5: the symbol specification shows swap type, swap long and short and the triple swap day; −6.2 points is $6.20 a night per lot
swap-mt5.caption: Find swap in MT5 under Specification. In points: swap per night = points × value of one point × lots (illustrative numbers).

swap-who.alt: Who pays swap in forex: scalpers and day traders who close before rollover pay none, swing traders should count it as a cost, carry traders may earn a positive swap
swap-who.caption: Day traders who close before the rollover never pay swap; swing traders should count it; a carry trade can earn it.

lev-margin.alt: Margin level, margin call and stop out: margin level is equity divided by used margin; as it falls the broker first warns you, then closes trades at the stop out level
lev-margin.caption: Margin level = equity ÷ used margin × 100%. As it falls you reach the margin call, then the stop out, where the broker closes trades.

lev-caps.alt: Forex leverage limits by regulator: 1:30 on major pairs in the EU and UK, 1:50 in the US, while offshore brokers often offer 1:500 or more
lev-caps.caption: Regulators cap retail leverage (1:30 EU and UK, 1:50 US); offshore brokers offer far more. Size trades from your risk, not the margin.

mt5-adds.alt: What MT5 adds over MT4: a built-in economic calendar, depth of market, hedging and netting modes, a 64-bit strategy tester, more timeframes and six pending order types
mt5-adds.caption: What MT5 adds: calendar, depth of market, hedging and netting, a faster tester, more timeframes and more order types.

mt-choose.alt: MT4 or MT5, which to choose: choose MT5 for a new account; stay on MT4 only if your broker or prop firm offers only MT4 or you need an MT4-only tool
mt-choose.caption: Choose MT5 for a new account; stay on MT4 only if your broker or prop firm requires it or you depend on an MT4-only tool.
